sections.heading: C2 — Before driving
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Before driving

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A27
Wear the shoulder belt across the chest and shoulder with very little slack. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A27
Do not route the shoulder belt beneath the arm. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A27
Do not route the shoulder belt behind the back. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A27
Incorrect shoulder-belt placement can cause serious internal injury in a crash. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A27
After fastening, tighten the lap belt low across the hips. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A27
An automatic shoulder belt still requires fastening the separate lap belt. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A27
Without the lap belt, a rider may slide out of an automatic shoulder belt in a collision. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A27
Sit upright with the back against the seat and the feet on the floor. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A27
Slouching or placing feet on the dashboard can reduce restraint effectiveness. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A27
Wear a safety belt even in a vehicle equipped with airbags. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A27
The handbook states that children below 14 must ride restrained in the rear seat while the vehicle moves. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A27
Airbags are supplemental restraints intended to work with safety belts. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A27
Airbags help reduce the chance of the head or upper body striking the vehicle interior. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A27
Airbags distribute crash forces across the body to help reduce serious injury. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A27
An airbag deploys once and deflates quickly, so it does not provide the same protection during a secondary collision. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A27
Safety belts position the body for airbag protection and restrain it in initial and later impacts. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A28
Front airbags are designed for frontal or near-frontal impacts. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R18 | anchor: A28
Front airbags are not designed to deploy for side impacts, rear impacts or rollovers. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R19 | anchor: A28
Rapid airbag inflation creates force that can injure someone contacting the deploying bag. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R20 | anchor: A28
Airbag-deployment injuries are usually minor burns or abrasions. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R21 | anchor: A28
Being very close to a deploying airbag can cause serious or fatal injury. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R22 | anchor: A28
In most vehicles, leave at least 10 inches between the chest center and the steering-wheel center. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R23 | anchor: A28
Consult the vehicle owner's manual for the correct seat adjustment with airbags. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R24 | anchor: A28
Raise the seat, use a cushion or lower the steering wheel as needed to aim the airbag toward the chest rather than the face. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R25 | anchor: A28
Keep hands on the outside of the steering wheel rather than across its airbag-deployment area. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R26 | anchor: A28
The handbook warns against seating a child in the right-front passenger position, especially beside an airbag. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R27 | anchor: A28
Children aged 12 or younger should sit in the back to avoid airbag injury. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R28 | anchor: A28
A front-passenger airbag switch, when provided, disables that airbag in its off position. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R29 | anchor: A28
The handbook describes the passenger-airbag off switch as intended for transporting a child aged 12 or younger in a vehicle without a suitable rear seat. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R30 | anchor: A28
Read the owner's manual for the airbag equipment specific to the vehicle. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R31 | anchor: A28
A child seat may fail to protect a child when incorrectly installed or used. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R32 | anchor: A28
Check that children aged 12 or younger are properly restrained in the rear seat. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R33 | anchor: A28
Never place a rear-facing child seat ahead of an active passenger airbag. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R34 | anchor: A28
Use both the vehicle manual and the restraint manufacturer's directions for child-restraint details. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0028]

Misconceptions: An airbag supplements a safety belt; its presence does not eliminate the need to buckle up.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: position, mirrors, restraints; use the cited facts for the actual setup and placement decisions.
Glossary: A head restraint limits rear-impact neck motion; front airbags are supplemental restraints; a shoulder harness is the upper belt portion.
Dynamic facts: Child-seat transition guidance and statutory age boundaries require issuer refresh; ambiguous mirror geometry and undated crash statistics remain typed debt.
